brief.headline: Neutral tape, energy leads; ASML damage and MSFT earnings demand attention
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits at 763.25, just 0.54% below its 50-day moving average and down 1.97% on the week. The 200-day gap is still +5.7%, so the longer trend is intact, but the near-term tape has softened. VIX at 18.53 is 16% above its 20-day moving average of 15.91, a caution signal without being a panic read. Breadth is the weak link: only 4 of 11 sectors (36%) are above their 50-day moving averages. Momentum leaders are entirely defensive and commodity-oriented (XLE, XLP, XLV, XLU), while XLK is the worst sector at -3.1% on 20-day momentum. Risk-on setups carry less conviction in this backdrop; the same breakout that would be straightforward in a broad rally now needs to prove itself against a narrow, rotating tape.

portfolio.note: Trading at 529.05, +1.7% above 20-day moving average with RSI 57.4 and a bullish DMA stack, but down 1.1% on the week and 4.0% off the 20-day high. Earnings land October 28. A miss or cautious guide in this softening tape could pressure the 40-day moving average at roughly 509.

Down 7.8% this week to 1641.52, now 6.8% below the 20-day moving average and 12.4% off the 20-day high of 1873.50. RSI is 37.7 with negative 20-day and 40-day momentum; DMA stack is mixed. EPS revisions remain positive (+7.5%) and forward P/E of 26.1x is only marginally above historical median, but price action has broken the structure. Earnings were due October 14, so any result reaction is already in the price. The thesis is intact fundamentally, but the technical damage warrants a review of position size against an ATR of 54.6 points.

At 68.24, just 0.07% off the 20-day high, with RSI at 70.0 and 20-day momentum of +6.7%. It is the top sector by momentum and benefits from crude oil pressing $98. RSI is approaching overbought, so watch for a pullback toward the 20-day moving average as a reset level.

At 382.01, GLD is 0.6% below its 20-day moving average with 20-day momentum of -4.8% and a mixed DMA stack. Gold futures (GC=F) show similar deterioration with RSI 44.2 and 40-day momentum of -10.5%. The position still carries a 66% unrealized gain, but the trend has turned negative near-term. Watch the 40-day moving average as the next structural level.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: ACN surged 10.7% this week to 229.68, pushing 16.9% above its 20-day moving average and 35.4% above the 100-day. Forward P/E is 14.5x with EPS revisions up 5.7% and revenue revisions up 5.3%. It is the highest-scoring name in the screen at 1.94. In a narrow, sector-rotating tape it is the rare large-cap showing genuine price leadership.
watchlist.risk: RSI at 73.4 and a 16.9% gap to the 20-day moving average mean any broad risk-off session could produce a sharp mean-reversion; the setup is extended entering a weak-breadth tape.

watchlist.name: Shopify Inc.
watchlist.thesis: SHOP is 7.4% above its 20-day moving average with 20-day momentum of +31.9% and strong relative strength versus the market (+31.7%). The DMA stack is bullish and earnings are November 3, creating a potential catalyst. Trailing P/E of 114.5x is a known premium, but price and momentum are aligned.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: ~158.00 implied. 20-day high: implied ~181. ATR-based stop distance: ~7.80 pts (4.6%).
watchlist.risk: High-multiple names get hit first in risk-off; a broad sell-off before the November 3 earnings date could erase the setup quickly.

watchlist.name: EOG Resources
watchlist.thesis: EOG rose 7.4% this week to 158.01, breaking out on volume (relative volume 1.83) with RSI 71.3 and 9.5% above its 20-day moving average. EPS revisions are up 4.4% and CY EPS growth is estimated at 75%. Energy is the top sector by 20-day momentum and crude at $97.97 underpins the thesis. Earnings November 5.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: ~144.30 implied. 20-day high: 158.37. ATR-based stop distance: ~3.58 pts (2.3%).
watchlist.risk: P/E is 15.1% above historical median; a crude reversal or disappointing OPEC signal breaks the setup.

watchlist.name: ConocoPhillips
watchlist.thesis: COP gained 9.3% this week to 146.51, 11.3% above its 20-day moving average and nearly at the 20-day high. EPS revisions are up 6.3% with CY growth estimated at 82.6%. Momentum confirms: +11.1% over 20 days.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: ~131.60 implied. 20-day high: 146.58. ATR-based stop distance: ~3.24 pts (2.2%).
watchlist.risk: P/E is 46.8% above historical median, the richest valuation flag in the energy screen; any crude demand concern would amplify the downside given stretched positioning.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC dropped 14.2% this week to 89.85, sitting 20.2% below its 20-day moving average and 29.5% off its 20-day high of 127.44. RSI is 31.4 and 20-day momentum is -17.3%. Forward P/E is 42.7x on estimated CY EPS of 1.53, a demanding multiple for a company in structural transition. Earnings arrive October 29.
watchlist.risk: An earnings beat or positive guidance could trigger a sharp short-covering bounce given the oversold RSI and 29.5% drawdown from recent highs.

watchlist.name: Novo Nordisk
watchlist.thesis: NVO is in a bearish DMA stack at 38.83, down 10.2% on 20-day momentum and 15.8% over 40 days. EPS estimates have been cut (-1.6%) and CY EPS growth is -2.8%. The pe_vs_hist flag of 2.25 stands out as an anomaly versus the price collapse, suggesting the market is already pricing in further estimate reductions. Earnings November 4.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: ~38.37 implied. 20-day high: ~41.15 implied. ATR-based stop distance: ~0.94 pts (2.4%).
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E has compressed to 9.1x; any positive clinical or regulatory news could create a violent snapback in a low-float ADR structure.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: WTI rose 4.5% this week to $97.97, sitting 5.3% above its 20-day moving average with RSI 58.3. Momentum is positive on both 20-day (+2.3%) and 40-day (+12.5%) frames. Watch the $100 level as the next psychological resistance and monitor inventory data for confirmation.

commodities.name: Brent Crude
commodities.note: Brent at $108.37 is in a full bullish DMA stack, 4.1% above its 20-day moving average with 20-day momentum of +8.0% and RSI 61.7. The spread over WTI is elevated, flagging geopolitical or supply-side premium that warrants watching.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold at $4,187 is 0.4% below its 20-day moving average with RSI 44.2 and 40-day momentum of -10.5%. The DMA stack has turned mixed. The prior trend of gold rising alongside equities has broken; a sustained move below the 40-day moving average near $4,338 would be a further negative signal for GLD holders.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Natural gas at $3.147 holds a bullish DMA stack with 20-day momentum of +11.0%, but it is 5.6% off its 20-day high and volume is thin (relative volume 0.10). Momentum is supportive for the energy trade but liquidity is a risk in any fast-moving session.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper at $6.60 is essentially flat on its 20-day moving average (RSI 51.1, 20-day momentum -1.3%) but shows very elevated relative volume of 4.82. Flat price with high volume often precedes a directional move; worth monitoring as a macro growth signal.

risks: MSFT earnings on October 28 and INTC on October 29 create binary risk in a tape where XLK is already the weakest sector by 20-day momentum (-3.1%).
VIX at 18.53 is 16% above its 20-day moving average of 15.91. Any escalation in the dominant theme driving energy prices could push volatility toward the low 20s quickly.
Breadth is thin: only 4 of 11 sectors above their 50-day moving averages. If energy or defensives roll over, there is no broad support underneath the index.
ASML's 7.8% weekly drop and breach of all moving averages is a warning signal for semi-cap equipment and could spread to related names if there is an industry-level demand concern.

Gold and silver are both in deteriorating trends (GC RSI 44, SI RSI 39, bearish DMA stack for silver). A flight-to-safety trade is not yet developing despite the softer equity tape, which is unusual and worth monitoring.
